mainTopic: Where the כהן גדול's bull stands on יום כיפור, which views count that spot as צפון, how סמיכה is done, and what an עולה atones for
overview: The משנה placed the כהן גדול's bull between the אולם and the מזבח for his וידוי, and the bull is slaughtered at that spot. A קרבן of this level must be slaughtered in the צפון, so the גמרא asks who counts this spot as צפון. It answers רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and brings a ברייתא with three widening views of צפון: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and רבי. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה could also follow רבי. It concludes that it can, because the specific spot was chosen to spare the weak, fasting כהן גדול extra walking. Next it explains how the bull's head can point south while its face points west: the bull stands north to south and turns its head. It does not stand straight east to west, so that it will not drop dung facing the מזבח. A ברייתא then describes how סמיכה and וידוי are done. רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא disagree about which sins an עולה atones for. The amud ends as רבי ירמיה begins to explain the root of their disagreement, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who holds that the area between the אולם and the מזבח counts as צפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא considers the area between the אולם and the מזבח to be צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whom have you heard who says that the area between the אולם and the מזבח counts as צפון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which Sage holds that the space between the אולם and the מזבח counts as צפון. This is the setup for the whole sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the bull stands between the אולם and the מזבח for the וידוי, and the bull is slaughtered where the וידוי is said. A קרבן of this level must be slaughtered in the צפון. So the משנה must hold this spot is צפון, and the גמרא wants to know whose view that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Whom have you heard (say this)? A formula asking which Sage holds a view
The Entrance Hall in front of the Sanctuary
The altar
The north side, where the holiest sacrifices must be slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה itself never says the word צפון. The question only arises because this bull must be slaughtered in the צפון, and it is slaughtered at the place of the וידוי.

phrases.english: Gemara: Whom have you heard
who says that the area between the Ulam and the altar is north?
phrases.notes: Based on Vayikra 1:11, 'on the side of the altar northward.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about where the bull stands during the וידוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as צפון.

steps.title: The answer: it is the view of רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the Sage: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. A ברייתא will be quoted next to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short answer that names who holds the view. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי, a תנא
It is (the view of)

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: A ברייתא with three views on how far צפון extends
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three expanding views of the צפון: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, then רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, then רבי. Everyone agrees the area from the חליפות inward is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: What is the צפון? From the northern wall of the מזבח until the wall of the courtyard, and also the area opposite the whole מזבח. These are the words of רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון adds even the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רבי adds even the place where the כהנים walk and even the place where ישראל walk. But everyone agrees that the area from the חליפות (chamber of knives) and inward is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as צפון. Along the way, it shows that רבי counts even more area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of three widening circles. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts only the area from the altar's north wall to the courtyard wall, plus the strip opposite the altar. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רבי adds even the walking areas of the כהנים and ישראל, which is basically the whole courtyard, except the side area of the חליפות that everyone rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The wall of the Temple courtyard
Adds (includes more area)
The place where the feet walk
The chamber of the slaughtering knives, an area off to the side
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: There are three widening views of צפון. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the narrowest. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון adds the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רבי adds the walking areas, almost the whole courtyard. All agree that the חליפות area is excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the map the rest of the sugya argues over. The next steps ask whether the משנה fits only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון or also רבי.

phrases.english: As it was taught: What is the north?
From the northern wall of the altar
until the wall of the courtyard,
and the area opposite the entire altar is also north;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon adds
even the area between the Ulam and the altar.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מוֹסִיף אַף מְקוֹם דְּרִיסַת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: Rabbi adds even the place where the Kohanim walk
and even the place where Yisrael walk.
But from the chamber of knives and inward,
everyone agrees that it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the answer in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts the area between the אולם and the מזבח as צפון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the views of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and רבי.

steps.title: Suggestion: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון and not רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and not רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say it is רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון, and not רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא floats an idea: maybe the משנה fits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון only, and not רבי. The next step will test this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 2 named רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the גמרא asks whether that answer is exclusive. The suggestion is that רבי, whose view is different, could not be the author of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? A tentative suggestion
רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
and not Rabbi?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא וְלָא רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the attribution in step 2 excludes רבי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה is limited to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and incompatible with רבי.

steps.title: Rejection: רבי includes everything רבי אלעזר includes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי adds on top of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's area too, so the משנה's spot is צפון for רבי as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it is רבי. Now, does רבי add only to רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה, and not to רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה could also follow רבי. רבי's wider צפון already includes the area between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's view is the widest circle, so it includes everything רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון counts. If רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would allow the spot in the משנה, רבי certainly would too. So nothing in the משנה excludes רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say
Now, i.e., is it reasonable that
On top of, in addition to

phrases.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi,
now, does Rabbi
add on top of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא מוֹסִיף?!
phrases.english: but not add on top of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's view includes רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's area, so the משנה's location is valid for רבי too.

steps.title: Clarified challenge: according to רבי, the bull could stand anywhere in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies its point. If the משנה followed רבי, why specify between the אולם and the מזבח? The bull could stand anywhere in the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we are saying: If it is רבי, let us stand the bull anywhere in the whole courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that it never meant רבי disagrees with the spot. Its point is that for רבי, the משנה had no reason to name such a specific spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether the spot is valid but why the משנה is so precise. For רבי almost the whole courtyard is צפון, so the משנה's specific location seems unnecessary. That precision seemed to point to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying, a clarification of an earlier question
Let us stand it (place the bull)
The entire courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: The question has changed. Step 4 asked whether רבי allows this spot. Now the question is why the משנה would pick this specific spot if רבי allows almost anywhere.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
If it is Rabbi,
let us stand it anywhere in the entire courtyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the suggestion of step 4 in a sharper form after the rejection in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי almost the whole courtyard is צפון, so the משנה's specific location would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Counter: the same problem exists for רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters that the same question applies to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. The bull could stand between the מזבח and the wall, which everyone agrees is צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? It is רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון? Then let us stand it between the altar and the wall!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. Even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון has other valid spots, so the specific location does not prove anything about who wrote the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area between the מזבח and the courtyard wall is צפון according to everyone. So for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too, the bull did not have to stand between the אולם and the מזבח. The משנה's choice must have another reason, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what (do you suggest)?
Between the altar and the courtyard wall

steps.whatToRemember: The specific spot in the משנה cannot decide between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Both had other valid locations, so the משנה must have a separate reason for its choice.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you suggest?
That it is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?
Then let us stand it between the altar and the wall!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge of step 6 back on the alternative attribution.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Using the משנה's specific location to prove it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and not רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון also had an alternative spot that everyone agrees is צפון, so the precision proves nothing.

steps.title: The real reason: the weakness of the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: Whatever answer רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would give, namely the weakness of the כהן גדול, רבי can give too. So the משנה fits רבי as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say about why the bull stands between the אולם and the מזבח? Because of the weakness of the כהן גדול. For רבי too, it is because of the weakness of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rebuttal from step 7. The specific spot was chosen to spare the tired, fasting כהן גדול extra walking, and that reason works for רבי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked: if the whole courtyard counts for רבי, why name a specific spot? Step 7 showed that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון faces the same question. Now the גמרא gives one shared answer: the spot was not chosen for legal validity but for the convenience of the כהן גדול. So the question proves nothing against רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: weakness
the High Priest
rather, what must you say? (introduces the answer both sides need)

steps.whatToRemember: The bull's spot between the אולם and the מזבח is a practical convenience for the weak כהן גדול. It is not a rule about where צפון begins, so the משנה can follow רבי too.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
Because of the weakness of the High Priest
phrases.notes: He is fasting and does all the service himself, so they spare him walking.

phrases.english: For Rabbi as well
it is because of the weakness of the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the counter-argument of step 7 by supplying the shared answer to step 6's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shared-reason answer: one practical explanation fits both opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The specific location in the משנה shows the author held that only that area counts as צפון, so the משנה cannot follow רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The location was chosen for the כהן גדול's comfort, so it says nothing about the boundaries of צפון. The משנה can follow רבי.

steps.title: How can the head face one way and the face another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'its head to the south and its face to the west' and asks how such a position is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: its head to the south and its face to the west. How can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and asks how it can be pictured. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A head and a face normally point the same way, so the description sounds contradictory. The גמרא asks for a realistic picture of the animal's position.

keyTerms.meaning: its head to the south
its face to the west
how can you find such a case?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'head' (ראש) and 'face' (פנים) are not the same thing. 'Head' describes the direction the body points. 'Face' is where the animal is looking.

phrases.english: Its head to the south and its face to the west.
How can you find this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צפון discussion and starts explaining a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A physical picture of an animal whose head points south while its face points west.

steps.title: רב: the bull turns its head
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the bull's body points south, but its head is turned so it faces west.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is a case where he turns its head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The bull stands lengthwise north to south, and its head is twisted to look west, toward the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Head to the south' describes the direction of the body. 'Face to the west' describes where the turned head looks. The two phrases describe two different things, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: bends, turns

phrases.english: Rav said: when he turns its head.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The body points north to south, and the head is turned westward.

steps.title: Why not just stand it facing west?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why twist the head? Just stand the whole bull straight, facing west.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us stand it straight (east-west, fully facing west).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's picture. If the goal is for the bull to face west, the whole animal could simply be lined up that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twisted position seems needlessly awkward. Lining the bull up east to west would point the whole animal toward the היכל without any twisting.

keyTerms.meaning: straight, outright

phrases.english: Let us stand it straight.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's explanation that the head is twisted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler position (fully east to west) gives the same result, so why require the awkward twist?

steps.title: אביי: to keep dung away from the altar
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the rabbis made a rule against lining the bull up east to west. In that position its rear would face the מזבח, and it might drop dung there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is a decree, lest it drop dung.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. If the bull faced fully west, its back end would point east toward the מזבח, and dung landing there would be a disgrace to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lining the bull up straight is not forbidden by Torah law. It is a rabbinic precaution (גזירה) to protect the honor of the מזבח. That is why the body points south and only the head turns west.

keyTerms.meaning: rabbinic protective decree
will drop dung

steps.whatToRemember: The bull points north to south with its head turned west. This keeps its rear away from the מזבח, out of respect for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a decree, lest it drop dung.
phrases.notes: Dung would land facing the altar, which is disrespectful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַרְבִּיץ גְּלָלִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic precaution explains the awkward position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull could just be lined up fully east to west.
steps.terutzMaskana: That position is avoided so the bull's rear does not face the מזבח.

steps.title: How סמיכה is done on an offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes סמיכה. The animal stands in the north facing west, and the person stands east of it, also facing west. He places both hands between its horns with nothing in between, and then confesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: How does one lean on the offering? The animal stands in the north, facing west. The one leaning stands in the east, facing west. He places his two hands between the two horns of the offering, as long as nothing separates him from the offering. And he confesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the exact procedure for סמיכה, connected to the כהן גדול leaning on his bull. It ends by saying he confesses, which sets up the next step about what he confesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא confirms that the animal faces west during סמיכה, just like the bull in our משנה. It adds two details: the hands go between the horns, and nothing may separate (חציצה) the hands from the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: the rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
leans his hands on the animal (סמיכה)
separates, blocks
confesses

steps.confusionAlert: Both the animal and the person face west. The person stands behind the animal (to its east), not opposite it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How does one lean on the offering?
It (the animal) stands in the north, its face to the west,
and the one leaning stands in the east, his face to the west,
and he places his two hands
between the two horns of the offering,
provided that nothing separates
between him and the offering,
and he confesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא on the procedure of סמיכה, which supports the westward facing in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In סמיכה, the animal stands in the north facing west. The person stands east of it facing west, places both hands between its horns with nothing in between, and confesses.

steps.title: What is confessed over each offering: רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: Over a חטאת one confesses the sin of a חטאת, and over an אשם the sin of an אשם. Over an עולה, says רבי יוסי הגלילי, one confesses failing to give the poor their gifts: לקט, שכחה, פאה, and מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Over a sin-offering, he confesses the sin of a sin-offering. Over a guilt-offering, the sin of a guilt-offering. Over a burnt-offering, the sin of gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, and the tithe for the poor. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now spells out what the person confesses. For חטאת and אשם it is obvious, but for an עולה רבי יוסי הגלילי names specific sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not say which sin an עולה atones for. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it covers not giving the poor their agricultural gifts. These are commands with no other penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: sin, transgression
the poor's gifts: fallen stalks, forgotten sheaves, the field's corner
the tithe given to the poor
a burnt-offering

phrases.english: Over a sin-offering, the sin of a sin-offering,
and over a guilt-offering, the sin of a guilt-offering,
and over a burnt-offering:

phrases.aramaic: עֲוֹן לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי,
phrases.english: the sin of gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner, and the poor man's tithe,
These are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, explaining the content of the confession mentioned at the end of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה atones for failing to give לקט, שכחה, פאה, and מעשר עני.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: an עולה covers positive commands
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. An עולה atones only for failing to do a positive command (עשה), or for breaking a prohibition that is fixed by a positive command (לאו הניתק לעשה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: A burnt-offering comes only for a positive command, and for a prohibition that is turned into a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a broader, more general rule than רבי יוסי הגלילי for which sins an עולה covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי named specific agricultural gifts. רבי עקיבא says the עולה covers every missed positive command, plus any prohibition that the Torah follows with a positive command to fix it. For example, stealing is fixed by returning the stolen item. These sins carry no court punishment, so the עולה brings atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: a positive command
a prohibition that is fixed by a follow-up positive command

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on what an עולה atones for. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the poor's agricultural gifts. רבי עקיבא says any missed עשה, plus any לאו הניתק לעשה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹלָה בָּאָה אֶלָּא עַל עֲשֵׂה,
phrases.english: A burnt-offering comes only for a positive command,
and for a prohibition that is transformed into a positive command.
phrases.notes: For example, the ban on stealing is followed by the command to return the stolen item.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין עוֹלָה בָּאָה אֶלָּא עַל עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing view to רבי יוסי הגלילי's list in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה atones only for a missed עשה and for a לאו הניתק לעשה.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle underlies the disagreement between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא about the עולה. It then introduces רבי ירמיה, who will answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree? רבי ירמיה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these two תנאים disagree about what an עולה atones for. This line is a setup. It only names רבי ירמיה, and his actual answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14 and 15 told us what each תנא holds, but not why. The גמרא is not challenging either side. It wants to find the deeper principle that splits them, so that the argument is about a reason and not just a list of sins.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?" This is a standard question that asks for the root principle behind an argument.
They disagree or argue.
An אמורא who will explain the basis of the disagreement.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for רבי ירמיה's answer in this line. Here the גמרא only says who will answer. The explanation itself comes right after.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
phrases.notes: This introduces the answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions given in Steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle or source makes רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא disagree about what an עולה atones for?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ירמיה gives the answer in the next part of the text.
